function.name: calculate_tip
function.description: Calculate the total tip amount for a given total bill and tip percentage. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

bill_total.description: The total bill amount. This is a float type value.

tip_percentage.description: The tip percentage. This is a float type value.

split.description: Number of people the tip is split between. Default is 1.

If you’re looking for the ultimate sushi experience in Los Angeles, **Sushi Gen** in West Hollywood is often hailed as the city’s top spot. Here’s why it stands out: | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Location** | 1020 N. Fairfax Ave., West Hollywood (close to Beverly Hills & Hollywood) | | **Ambiance** | Elegant yet intimate setting with a modern Japanese aesthetic; perfect for both casual meals and special occasions | | **Chef** | Chef Masahiro “Masa” Sato, a Michelin‑starred chef who brings meticulous precision and creative flair to every roll | | **Signature Dishes** | • *Omakase* tasting menu (seasonal, 12‑course)
• *Tuna Tataki* with citrus vinaigrette
• *Uni (sea urchin)* from local farms | | **Quality** | Fresh, sustainably sourced fish; daily deliveries from the Pacific; meticulous plating | | **Service** | Attentive, knowledgeable staff who explain each dish and recommend pairings | | **Price Range** | $80–$120 per person for the omakase; $20–$35 for à la carte items | | **Reservations** | Highly recommended; book at least 2–3 weeks in advance via their website or phone | ### Why It’s Considered the Best 1. **Chef’s Reputation** – Masa Sato’s Michelin star and years of experience in Tokyo set a high standard for quality and innovation. 2. **Freshness** – The restaurant sources fish directly from local fishermen and international suppliers, ensuring peak freshness. 3. **Omakase Experience** – The tasting menu offers a curated journey through seasonal flavors, showcasing the chef’s artistry. 4. **Atmosphere** – The sleek, minimalist décor creates an immersive dining environment that feels both upscale and welcoming. ### Alternatives Worth Checking Out | Restaurant | Highlights | |------------|------------| | **Sushi Zo** (West Hollywood) | Known for its “sushi bar” concept and a wide variety of nigiri and rolls. | | **Sushi Taro** (Beverly Hills) | Offers a more traditional Japanese feel with a focus on sashimi. | | **KazuNori** (Hollywood) | A hidden gem with a relaxed vibe and creative rolls. | | **Sushi Gen** (West Hollywood) | The top pick for Michelin‑starred quality and an unforgettable omakase. | ### Tips for Visiting - **Dress Code:** Smart casual is recommended; some restaurants have a dress code for the omakase experience. - **Timing:** Lunch hours (12–2 pm) can be less crowded, but the omakase is usually served in the evening. - **Special Requests:** If you have dietary restrictions or preferences, let the staff know when booking; they’re usually accommodating. Enjoy your sushi adventure in LA! If you need help with reservations or want to explore other neighborhoods, just let me know.
